title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-22
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 4♠. It looks as though only 3 losers exist, the ♠A, a heart trick, and a diamond trick. If South ruffs the second heart lead and tries to knock out the ♠A, East will duck the first 2 spade tricks.

If South continues spades, East will take his ♠A and play another heart, forcing South's last trump. East will now have a second trump trick and the contract will fail. South can guard against a 4-1 trump break by discarding a diamond at trick 2. South has a diamond loser anyway and by losing it early, he is able to retain trump control.

If the defense continues hearts, dummy (now being void) can trump. Assume the defense switches to clubs and South wins. South plays trump, East holding up as before. South now has one more trump than East. South can trump the heart return and draw East's last trump. South has all winners remaining.
